Emmitt Smith.text: The only running back to win the Super Bowl, NFL MVP, rushing crown and Super Bowl MVP in one season.
Emmitt Smith.evidence: Smith is the only running back to ever win a Super Bowl championship, the NFL Most Valuable Player award, the NFL rushing crown, and the Super Bowl Most Valuable Player award all in the same season (1993).

Walter Payton.text: The running back also threw eight career touchdown passes.
Walter Payton.evidence: Payton also retired with the most receptions by a non-receiver, and he threw eight career touchdown passes.

Frank Gore.text: Holds the league record for games played by a running back.
Frank Gore.evidence: His career was also noted for longevity, a rare trait with his position, and he holds the league record for games played by a running back.

Barry Sanders.text: Retired unexpectedly at 31, just 1,457 yards short of Walter Payton's career rushing record.
Barry Sanders.evidence: While still performing at a high level, Sanders unexpectedly retired from professional football in 1999, at the age of 31, and 1,457 yards short of breaking the NFL's then all-time rushing record held by Walter Payton.

Adrian Peterson.text: Tore his ACL and MCL in late 2011, then ran for 2,097 yards the next season.
Adrian Peterson.evidence: Peterson tore both his anterior cruciate and medial collateral ligaments in a game in late 2011. Despite that, he returned by the start of the 2012 season, and ended it with 2,097 rushing yards, just nine yards shy of breaking Eric Dickerson's single-season record.

Curtis Martin.text: Only started playing football in his senior year of high school, at his mother's insistence.
Curtis Martin.evidence: At the insistence of his mother, who wanted him to participate in an extracurricular activity as a way to keep him away from crime and violence, Curtis began to play football during his senior year, despite having never cared much for the sport.

LaDainian Tomlinson.text: Set the single-season record for touchdowns, 31, in his 2006 MVP season.
LaDainian Tomlinson.evidence: Tomlinson's output reached a peak in 2006, when he set numerous single-season records, including for most touchdowns scored (31). These feats won him the NFL MVP award, but San Diego suffered an upset defeat in their playoff opener, and Schottenheimer was fired shortly afterwards.

Jerome Bettis.text: Did not play football until high school; as a youth, his main passion was bowling.
Jerome Bettis.evidence: Bettis did not start playing football until high school, as his primary passion as a youth had been bowling.

Derrick Henry.text: The only player to rush for 2,000 yards in a season at the high school, college and pro levels.
Derrick Henry.evidence: Noted for his success at every stage of his career, Henry is the only player to have rushed for at least 2,000 yards in a season at the high school, college, and professional levels.

Eric Dickerson.text: Wore prescription goggles throughout his career because of myopia.
Eric Dickerson.evidence: Dickerson wore prescription goggles throughout his career due to myopia.
